summary:
AEGIS-X HEALTH is an autonomous astronaut self-evaluation and triage web application designed to monitor crew health and deliver actionable emergency protocols during deep space missions. Built with a futuristic, mission ready interface, the platform tracks critical physiological biometrics including heart rate, radiation exposure, and immune markers while running real time anomaly detection and interactive diagnostic simulations.

As human spaceflight pushes beyond Low Earth Orbit toward the Moon and Mars, communication delays with Mission Control can exceed 20 minutes each way, making real-time Earth based medical intervention impossible. AEGIS-X HEALTH bridges this critical gap by empowering crews to rapidly assess medical emergencies, receive step by step triage guidance, and stabilize acute conditions independently. By combining continuous biometric telemetry with automated clinical decision support, our solution reduces cognitive load during high stress crises and safeguards astronaut survival on long duration exploration missions.
details:
What it does: Aegis-X is an on-board health copilot for astronauts on missions where Earth is too far away to help in time. It combines simulated wearable vitals, cabin air and radiation readings, a self-administered reaction test and a daily check-in into a personal health index for each crew member. Every reading is judged against that astronaut’s own baseline. When a hazard appears (a CO₂ leak, a solar storm, an immune shift or extreme fatigue) it shows what is happening, gives the crew a tickable checklist, and recommends who is fittest for each job: spacewalk, robotic arm, exercise or routine work. It also tracks limited medical supplies, shows a live dose clock for radiation absorbed versus avoided by sheltering, and writes a structured SBAR report for the flight surgeon.

  • The habitat map — a live SVG floor plan where crew members’ dots physically move into the storm shelter as the scenario unfolds. That’s a strong, demo-friendly visual that belongs in “What it does” or “Creativity” — judges remember things they can watch happen, not just read about.
  • Accessibility — the dashboard is now fully keyboard-navigable (crew selection, not just mouse) and respects reduced-motion settings. Space Apps judging criteria include impact/inclusivity, so a one-line mention costs nothing and helps.

Benefits and impact: On a Mars mission the signal delay can reach about 44 minutes round trip, so the crew must act first and inform Earth second. Aegis-X supports fast, personal, autonomous decisions and keeps Earth informed with a clear handoff.

NASA connection: The design follows the NASA Human Research Program’s hazards of spaceflight: radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity and closed environments.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, Tailwind CSS and Chart.js, hosted as a single-page web app. No special hardware is needed.

Creativity: Instead of a passive dashboard, Aegis-X decides and acts. It ranks the crew for each task, links checklist steps to supply use, and simulates the delayed reply from Earth.

Factors considered: Personal baselines, communication delay, limited supplies, crew workload and radiation exposure.

Limitations: All data is simulated and thresholds are illustrative. This is a prototype concept, not medical advice or official NASA procedure.

(The solar storm scenario is modeled on the real May 2024 solar storm documented by NASA Goddard using Solar Dynamics Observatory data.)
dataRefs: NASA Human Research Program: Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight
